text.text: Childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33 are associated with low lung function trajectory into early adulthood.
Lower childhood lung function may causally increase plasma CXCL10.
IL33 merits further investigation as a therapeutic target to prevent COPD.

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) affects over 200 million people worldwide and causes approximately 3 million deaths each year. 1 While smoking remains the chief risk factor for COPD, over 25% occurs in never-smokers, with aetiology increasingly recognised as reflecting complex interactions between environmental exposure and individual susceptibility. 2, 3 Over half of cases arise from low lung function trajectories established early in life, for which the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. 4, 5 COPD incidence is strongly age-associated, with variation in biological ageing proposed as a potential driver of disease susceptibility. 6 Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA), derived from so-called 'epigenetic clocks' applied to DNA methylation data, is one measure of biological ageing associated with lower adult lung function and COPD. 7 Although EAA is associated with other adverse outcomes in childhood and adolescence, its relevance to low early-life lung function trajectories remains unknown. 8, 9 While the therapeutic relevance of EAA to COPD is also yet to be established, cellular senescence, an ageing process involving irreversible cell cycle arrest and secretion of inflammatory mediators, has been mechanistically linked to disease pathogenesis. 10 Plasma concentrations of proteins forming the 'senescence-associated secretory phenotype' are associated with lung function; such proteins may represent promising therapeutic targets if causally implicated. [10] [11] [12] Mendelian randomisation (MR) uses genetic variants associated with exposures of interest as instrumental variables to estimate causal effects on outcomes, mitigating confounding and reverse causation. 13 Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of epigenetic and proteomic ageing biomarkers permit MR analyses of whether accelerated biological ageing is causally implicated in adverse earlylife lung function trajectories. 14, 15 In this study, we combine conventional epidemiological and MR approaches in a large UK birth cohort to assess whether EAA and senescence-associated plasma proteins causally affect the risk of low lung function trajectories from childhood to early adulthood.

text.text: Our study identified observational associations of childhood plasma concentrations of CXCL10, IL6 and IL33 with Persistently Low lung function trajectory into early adulthood, but there was little evidence that EAA was associated with longitudinal patterns of lung function.

MR analyses did not identify causal effects from plasma proteins on lung function trajectory or mean longitudinal lung function, but reverse MR suggested lower childhood lung function may causally increase plasma levels of CXCL10.

These findings suggest that elevated circulating CXCL10 is a downstream marker of lung pathology in childhood rather than a causal determinant, although pleiotropy in reverse MR remains a possibility given the polygenic instrument for FEV1 derived from adult GWAS, its association with childhood BMI, and some inconsistency across two-sample MR estimators.

Given the lack of evidence for a causal effect of IL6 on longitudinal lung function and trend towards an inverse causal effect of childhood FEV1 on IL6, the observational association for IL6 may also reflect reverse causation and/or confounding.
Although a weak genetic instrument precluded assessment of the causal effect of IL33, there was limited evidence that childhood FEV1 causally influenced IL33.
Overall, we did not identify evidence of a causal role for these plasma proteins in low lung function trajectories, although limited statistical power precludes definitive conclusions.

Our findings are consistent with previous observational studies reporting positive associations of CXCL10 and IL6 with adverse early-life lung function trajectories, 12 and identify IL33 as a novel biomarker.

text.text: Alternatively, epigenetic clocks trained in older adults (except the paediatric Wu clock) may fail to capture biological variation relevant to lung health in this age group.
EAA measured in blood rather than lung tissue may also be less relevant to lung pathology and dysfunction.

Together, the absence of clear associations between childhood EAA and lung function trajectory, pleiotropic nature of senescence-associated plasma proteins, and lack of evidence from MR do not lend support to accelerated biological ageing or cellular senescence as causal processes in early-life lung function impairment.

However, our evidence that impaired early-life lung function is causally related to persistent elevation in circulating inflammatory proteins should prompt further research into whether 'inflammatory overspill' from the lung might help explain increased subsequent multimorbidity in individuals with low lung function trajectories. 39 Additionally, the biological plausibility of IL33 as a causal mediator and recent positive clinical trial evidence for IL33 antagonists in COPD mean it should be assessed as a potential early therapeutic target to prevent COPD in individuals with high-risk lung function trajectories. 34 Strengths of this study include repeated lung function measurements enabling longitudinal trajectory modelling, integration of multi-omic biomarkers and triangulation between observational and bidirectional MR analyses.

text.text: Limitations include low statistical power for MR, restricting capacity to detect modest causal effects.
Epigenetic clocks were largely derived in adult populations, limiting their interpretability in this age group.
Our complete-case analysis may be subject to selection bias.
Although our trajectory modelling approach has been shown to successfully predict later-life airflow obstruction, the health implications of membership of lower trajectory groups remains uncertain.
The predominantly white European study population limits generalisability.
In conclusion, childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33, but not EAA, were associated with low lung function trajectory into early adulthood.
MR identified no causal effects from proteins on longitudinal lung function but suggested lower childhood lung function may cause persistently higher plasma CXCL10.

Future research should further investigate IL33 as a potential early therapeutic target in adverse lung function trajectories and assess persistent systemic inflammation as a mediator for associated multimorbidity.

Primary one-sample MR analyses used two-stage residual inclusion (2SRI), with ageing biomarkers (epigenetic or proteomic) as exposure and membership of the lowest, or two lowest, trajectory groups treated as a binary outcome.

To increase statistical power in MR, a secondary analysis incorporated two-stage least squares (2SLS) MR with a proxy continuous outcome: the time-weighted mean FEV1 (% predicted) over follow-up (area under the curve per time; FEV1 % AUC/time).
Estimates were compared to those from observational ordinary least squares (OLS) regression.

To investigate reverse causation, we also compared 2SLS MR and OLS estimates of childhood FEV₁ and asthma diagnosis (parental report/relevant medication at age 7 or 8) (exposure) on ageing biomarkers (outcome).
All MR models, and observational models fitted for comparison, were adjusted for sex and genetic principal components 1-10 and included complete cases.
Continuous exposure and outcome variables were standardised, with prior log transformation of IL6 ELISA measurements due to right skew.

Satisfaction of the core assumptions of MR was evaluated through F statistics gauging the relevance of genetic instruments to exposures, regression modelling to assess independence of genetic instruments from measured confounders, and application of two-sample MR methods to evaluate violation of exclusion restriction by pleiotropy in multi-SNP instruments.

Two-sample MR methods included inverse-variance weighted (IVW), weighted median, weighted mode and MR-Egger, with estimates for SNP-exposure associations taken from external GWAS and SNP-outcome associations estimated in ALSPAC.
To limit potential pleiotropy, primary proteomic MR analyses used cis-protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs) within 10Mb of the gene encoding each protein or its receptor.
